cse-2006-cs-24.approach: Look only at the elements of $A \cup B$. Under a uniformly random permutation, each of them is equally likely to receive the smallest image; the condition holds exactly when that element lies in $A \cap B$.

steps.title: When are the minima equal?
steps.body:
Let $e$ be the element of $A \cup B$ with the smallest image $\pi(e)$. Then $\min \pi(A \cup B) = \pi(e)$.

- If $e \in A \cap B$: $\min\pi(A) = \min\pi(B) = \pi(e)$.
- If $e \in A \setminus B$: $\min\pi(A) = \pi(e) < \min\pi(B)$, so they differ (similarly for $B \setminus A$).

So the condition holds iff $e \in A \cap B$.

steps.title: Symmetry
steps.body:
By symmetry every element of $A \cup B$ is equally likely to be $e$, so
$$P(e \in A\cap B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}.$$

steps.body: Number of permutations $= n! \cdot \dfrac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}$.

steps.title: Rounds
steps.body: A 64-byte block starting at 0 needs $\lceil 64/48 \rceil = 2$ rounds (48 B, then the remaining 16 B from banks 0–7).

steps.title: Latency
steps.body: Per round: $k/2 + 80 = 12 + 80 = 92$ ns. Total $= 2 \times 92 = 184$ ns.

optionAnalysis.reason: Wrong: 92 ns is one round only; 48 B < 64 B.
Wrong: 104 ns $= 12 + 92$ counts the second decode but not the second 80 ns access.
Wrong: 172 ns $= 12 + 2\times80$ decodes only once.
Correct: two rounds of $12 + 80$ ns.

pitfalls: Forgetting that each round needs its own decode time.

cse-2006-cs-42.approach: Each conditional branch blocks fetch until stage 3 resolves it, costing 2 stall cycles; add the stall cycles to the 1 cycle per instruction baseline.

steps.title: Branch penalty
steps.body: The branch is fetched in stage 1 and resolved at the end of stage 3. The next instruction can be fetched only after that, so stages 2 and 3 of the branch pass with no new fetch: penalty $= 3 - 1 = 2$ cycles.

steps.title: Total cycles
steps.body:
Baseline: $10^9$ cycles. Branches: $0.2 \times 10^9 = 2 \times 10^8$, each adds 2 cycles: $4 \times 10^8$.

Total $= 10^9 + 4 \times 10^8 = 1.4 \times 10^9$ cycles.

steps.title: Time
steps.body: At 1 GHz a cycle is 1 ns: $1.4 \times 10^9 \times 10^{-9} = 1.4$ s.

optionAnalysis.reason: Wrong: ignores the branch stalls.
Wrong: uses a 1-cycle penalty ($1 + 0.2 \times 1$).
Correct: $1 + 0.2 \times 2 = 1.4$ cycles per instruction.
Wrong: uses a 3-cycle penalty ($1 + 0.2 \times 3$).

animation.caption: I2 is fetched only after I1 finishes stage 3 — 2 bubble cycles

cse-2006-cs-43.approach: To test a single bit with AND, the mask must have a 1 exactly at position `pos` and 0 elsewhere — that is `1 << pos`.

steps.title: Required mask
steps.body: `temp = reg & mask` is non-zero iff some bit set in `mask` is also set in `reg`. To depend on bit `pos` only, `mask` must be $2^{pos}$, i.e. `0x1 << pos`.

steps.title: Check example
steps.body: `pos = 3`: `mask = 0b1000`. For `reg = 0b1010`, `temp = 0b1000 ≠ 0` → branch (bit 3 is 1). For `reg = 0b0111`, `temp = 0` → no branch.

optionAnalysis.reason: Correct: single 1 at position `pos`.
Wrong: `0xffffffff >> pos` keeps the low $32-pos$ bits, so any set low bit triggers the branch.
Wrong: `pos` itself is a small number (e.g. 3 = 0b11), testing bits 0 and 1 instead of bit 3.
Wrong: `0xf` always tests bits 0–3, independent of `pos`.

cse-2006-cs-43.verification: For `pos = 3`, `reg = 0b0001`: (A) gives 0 (correct, bit 3 clear); (B) and (D) give non-zero (wrong).

cse-2006-cs-44.approach: The optimal window keeps the pipe full for one round trip: window = bandwidth × RTT / packet size.

optionAnalysis.reason: Wrong: 20 uses the one-way delay (40 ms) instead of the round trip.
Correct: $1280\,\text{B} / 32\,\text{B} = 40$.
Wrong: 160 would be the bandwidth–delay product in 8-byte units (or in bits divided by 64).
Wrong: 320 divides bits by 32 (treats packets as 32 bits).

pitfalls: Mixing bits and bytes: 32-byte packets are 256 bits; $10240/256 = 40$.
